newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SEC approves mutual fund amendment - NASDAQ.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SEC approves mutual fund amendment - NASDAQ.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission approved an amendment to an existing mutual fund regulation that will allow listing for about an additional 1,400 small mutual funds and money market funds, NASDAQ said Monday.

The rule, approved on December 16, will enable those funds to be included in the Mutual Fund Quotation Service, NASDAQ said in a statement. Previously, small funds needed to have 300 fund shareholders at the time of application.

The amended rule eliminates the shareholder requirement and replaces it with two alternative standards: either have net assets at the time of application of $10 million or more; or have been in operation for two years.
The amended rule was first proposed by the National Association of Securities Dealers on October 18.
NASDAQ stock market disseminates two lists daily containing the net asset values of over 5,000 mutual funds: the News Media List and the Supplemental List.
The amended regulation does not affect the News Media List, which consists of data for about 5,500 funds, according to the statement.
NASDAQ will begin accepting applications for inclusion in the Supplemental List beginning February 3, 1997. This list contains data for more than 450 mutual funds.
The stock market will also make mutual fund prices available on its internet site at www.nasdaq.com in early January. Price will be updated daily.
